records.quote: Corollary 4.13. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18), where Σ1 and Σ2 are correlation matrices. Then Y1 ≤sm Y2 if and only if µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
records.model: other: multivariate GLSE random vectors (location-scale-skew model (18))
records.compared: Y1 vs Y2 in the supermodular order, parameterized by correlation matrices

hypotheses.text: Σ1, Σ2 correlation matrices; µ1 = µ2; δ1 = δ2; σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤sm Y2 iff the stated equalities and correlation inequalities hold

records.ambiguity: sm (supermodular) is not in the plain-order vocabulary → 'other: sm' (B's label correct, A's bare 'sm' not in allowed list).

note: Printed iff characterization of ≤sm for GLSE vectors with correlation matrices; labeled 'other: sm'.

records.quote: Lemma 4.14. (Müller and Scarsini, 2000) Let X, Y be two bivariate random vectors and have the same marginals, then X ≤sm Y is equivalent to X ≤uo Y.
records.family: arbitrary bivariate vectors (cited result, not GLSE-specific)
records.compared: X vs Y; supermodular and upper orthant orders

hypotheses.text: X, Y bivariate random vectors with the same marginals

conclusion.direction: X ≤sm Y ⟺ X ≤uo Y in the bivariate case

records.ambiguity: Quoted result used to bridge sm and uo orders; neither order is in the plain vocabulary.

note: Printed bivariate sm⟺uo equivalence (Müller–Scarsini); labeled 'other: sm/uo equivalence'.

records.quote: Theorem 4.12. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). Y1 ≤sm Y2 if and only if Y1 and Y2 have the same marginals and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
records.compared: Y1 vs Y2 in the supermodular order

hypotheses.text: Y1, Y2 have the same marginals (µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2, σ1,ii = σ2,ii) and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n
hypotheses.formal: equal marginals + covariance ordering — iff characterization

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤sm Y2 iff same marginals and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij (i < j)

records.quantifiers: all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n; all supermodular f

note: Printed iff supermodular characterization; 'other: sm' label per vocabulary.

records.quote: Theorem 4.15. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ2 + β(z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + β(z)δ1 for all z, σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n and σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ n, then Y1 ≤uo Y2.
records.compared: Y1 vs Y2 in the upper orthant order — sufficient conditions

hypotheses.text: µ2 + β(z)δ2 ≥ µ1 + β(z)δ1 for all z; σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all i; σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all i ≠ j
hypotheses.formal: pointwise location-mixture ordering + equal variances + covariance ordering

records.quantifiers: all z; all 1 ≤ i ≤ n; all 1 ≤ i ≠ j ≤ n

records.quote: (2) If Y1 ≤uo Y2 and g satisfies Assumption 4.1, then µ1 + E(β(Z))δ1 ≤ µ2 + E(β(Z))δ2 and σ1,ii = σ2,ii for all 1 ≤ i ≤ n.
records.compared: necessary consequences of the upper orthant order

hypotheses.text: Y1 ≤uo Y2 and g satisfies Assumption 4.1
hypotheses.formal: uo order assumed; mixing density g meets Assumption 4.1

conclusion.direction: Y1 ≤uo Y2 (as hypothesis) ⇒ componentwise Y1,i ≤st Y2,i and the printed mean/variance consequences

records.ambiguity: Necessity direction: the uo order is the premise here.

records.quote: (3) If Y1 and Y2 have the same marginals and Y1 ≤uo Y2, then σ1,ij ≤ σ2,ij for all 1 ≤ i < j ≤ n.
records.compared: necessary covariance ordering from the uo order

hypotheses.text: Y1, Y2 have the same marginals and Y1 ≤uo Y2

records.ambiguity: Proof prints '(Y1,i, Y1,j)ᵀ ≤uo (Y1,i, Y1,j)ᵀ' and '≤sm (Y1,i, Y1,j)ᵀ' — both compare a vector to itself; evidently typos for (Y2,i, Y2,j)ᵀ.

note: Multi-part theorem split into three records; 'uo' is a paper-defined orthant order → 'other: uo'. Proof of part 3 has a self-comparison typo.

records.quote: Theorem 4.16. Let Y1, Y2 follow (18). The following statements are true: (1) If µ1 = µ2, δ1 = δ2 and Σ2 − Σ1 is copositive, then Y1 ≤cp Y2.
